analysis.title: GS Pasquariello - markets / macro 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: Pasquariello says the AI trade has entered a more complicated phase for both credit and equity markets, centered on the availability and cost of capital.

The shift in AI narrative challenged consensus positions and triggered a significant round of risk reduction. He cites the CPI data, higher highs in deferred Brent contracts, and strong earnings not being rewarded (ASML, TSMC) as possible catalysts.

GS basket of AI credit spreads (GSUCHS30) gapped out to the wides of the year. The AI leaders-vs-laggards basket was up nearly 100% YTD at the end of June, and all of that performance has since been given back.
The gap between perceived high quality and low quality assets is widening. HY is underperforming IG, and the GS high quality vs low quality pair trade (GSP1QUAL) rose sharply over the past month.

NDX went 0-5 on the week and the S&P dropped 2%, losing the escape velocity from its early October breakout from a multi-month consolidation. The GS hedge VIP pair trade (GSTHVIPP) had its worst week since the depths of COVID.

Since the Iran war began, the market's central tension has been strong earnings growth against headwinds from energy and interest rates. Recently the market has struggled because of a gathering consensus that large upward estimate revisions are behind us, and because higher rates came into play.

For the first time in three years, several asset markets (high velocity stocks, high yield credit, some sovereign bond markets) felt the 'speed limit' from the bond market. The backup in rates was arrested late in the week.

Cyclicals continue to struggle. RTY broke down through its 200-day moving average, BKX did the same despite fine Q3 earnings, and CAT, VRT and GEV charts are weak. The question is whether the downgrade to the growth outlook has gone far enough.

Flows were decisively risk-off, with supply from both long-only money and hedge funds. This was the single largest week of net tech selling in at least a decade, skewed to semis. Recent weeks saw the largest supply in global AI stocks since the launch of ChatGPT, taking exposure to the 35th percentile of the past year.

Options showed anxiety: VIX rose to 20 (+5 points w/w), the front of the VIX futures curve is inverted, VIX call volume was very significant, and notional traded in S&P puts was a record. He says the market is cleaner than it was a few weeks ago.

He expects a few more pockets of supply toward month-end (mutual fund fiscal year-end, risk reduction ahead of the midterms). After that, corporate buybacks should become the dominant technical, and November is the second largest month of the year for buybacks.
The key fundamental question is whether Q3 earnings can restore confidence. META on Wednesday is the first pressure test.

He is still inclined to think the choppiness of September and October will give way to strength in November and December. He had been arguing for long stocks paired with short bonds and says that position was hurt this week.

sector_views.rationale: Largest week of net tech selling in at least a decade, skewed to semis, with AI leaders basket giving back all of its YTD gains.
RTY and BKX broke below the 200-day moving average, and CAT, VRT and GEV charts are weak under higher energy costs and rates.

earnings_insights: Q3 earnings: Pasquariello calls the first pressure test META on Wednesday (reporting date per the note, not a result).
ASML and TSMC reported strong earnings that were not rewarded by the market (reported, per the note, no figures given).
BKX had a 'totally fine' round of Q3 earnings (reported) but still broke below its 200-day moving average.

tension_points.theme: earnings strength vs rates and energy
tension_points.bull_case: Superb earnings growth has been the north star for the market for four years and buoyed it through Q1 and Q2. Buybacks should dominate in November, and he expects strength in November and December.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher energy costs and higher interest rates have taken a real toll. There is a gathering consensus that large upward estimate revisions are behind us, and strong earnings (ASML, TSMC) were not rewarded.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 earnings failing to restore confidence, with META on Wednesday as the first pressure test.
